enhanced.fullText:
The Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007 (FDAAA), codified as Public Law No. 110-85, significantly expanded FDA regulatory authority over clinical trials and established mandatory registration and results reporting requirements for certain clinical investigations. Under 42 U.S.C. § 282(j) and implementing regulations at 42 CFR Part 11, higher education institutions conducting FDA-regulated clinical trials must comply with comprehensive registration, informed consent, and data reporting obligations.

The Act requires sponsors and principal investigators of "applicable clinical trials" to register studies on ClinicalTrials.gov within 21 days of enrollment of the first participant. Applicable clinical trials include controlled studies of FDA-regulated drugs, biological products, or devices involving human subjects, conducted under investigational new drug applications (21 CFR Part 312) or investigational device exemptions (21 CFR Part 812). Universities conducting such research must ensure compliance regardless of funding source, though federally-funded projects face additional oversight.

Critical informed consent requirements under 21 CFR § 50.25 mandate that consent forms include specific language notifying participants that trial information will be submitted to ClinicalTrials.gov. The regulation states that "a description of this clinical trial will be available on http://www.ClinicalTrials.gov, as required by U.S. Law. This Web site will not include information that can identify you." Participants who refuse this data submission cannot participate in covered trials.

Universities must establish robust compliance mechanisms as violations carry severe penalties. Under 21 U.S.C. § 333, willful violations may result in criminal prosecution, fines up to $250,000 for individuals and $1,000,000 for institutions, and potential debarment from federal contracting. The FDA may also issue warning letters, impose clinical holds under 21 CFR § 312.42, and pursue injunctive relief.

Institutional Review Boards must verify FDAAA compliance during initial and continuing review processes. The 2017 Clinical Trials Registration and Results Information Submission Rule (82 Fed. Reg. 12526) expanded requirements to include summary results reporting within one year of study completion, with potential civil monetary penalties up to $10,000 per day for non-compliance under 42 U.S.C. § 282(j)(5)(A).

Universities must designate responsible parties for registration, maintain accurate trial records, and ensure principal investigators understand their legal obligations under this comprehensive regulatory framework governing clinical research integrity and transparency.
enhanced.summary: The FDA Amendments Act of 2007 requires universities conducting clinical trials of investigational drugs and devices to register studies on ClinicalTrials.gov, obtain specific informed consent for data submission, and comply with comprehensive reporting requirements under federal law.
enhanced.requirements:
## Clinical Trial Registration
- Register applicable clinical trials on ClinicalTrials.gov within 21 days of first participant enrollment per 42 CFR § 11.22
- Designate responsible party for registration and data accuracy
- Update registration information within 30 days of any changes

## Informed Consent Requirements
- Include mandatory ClinicalTrials.gov disclosure language in all consent forms per 21 CFR § 50.25
- Ensure participants understand data submission requirements before enrollment
- Exclude participants who refuse data submission consent

## IRB Oversight Obligations
- Verify FDAAA compliance during initial protocol review
- Monitor ongoing compliance through continuing review processes
- Ensure investigators understand registration and reporting obligations

## Results Reporting
- Submit summary results within 12 months of study completion per 42 U.S.C. § 282(j)
- Maintain accurate and complete trial records
- Designate qualified personnel for data submission responsibilities
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Register trials within 21 days of first enrollment on ClinicalTrials.gov. Update registration within 30 days of protocol changes. Submit summary results within 12 months of study completion. Maintain continuous data accuracy throughout trial duration per 42 CFR Part 11.
